newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine truckers end 600-mile highway protest.
newsitem.headline: Argentine truckers end 600-mile highway protest.

text.p: A convoy of 2,500 trucks ended a three-day protest on Argentine highways on Tuesday with threats of further disruption if their demands for laws to protect them from foreign competition are not heeded.

"If we are not heard we will continue these protests and stoppages on the borders," said truckers' leader Hugo Moyano, after the 600-mile (1,000-km) protest ended at the Roman Catholic pilgrimage centre of Lujan, near Buenos Aires.

A convoy 40 miles (70 km) long left the northwestern city of Mendoza on Sunday loaded with goods including gasoline, livestock, cereal, fruit and vegetables. It crawled along highways, holding up traffic, to protest against competition from trucking firms from neighbouring countries.
The truckers' union has threatened to call a 14-day strike that would block border crossings if the government does not draft a special transportation law protecting their jobs.
